setup.why: route needs the INTEGER test_case_id, not the TC-NNNN identifier; resolved TC-54455 and TC-54456 to their integer ids

attempts.changed: Well-formed request with the correct integer ids (project, folder, and the case known to carry attachment 1102622); still a bare 500. Retried against a second, sibling test case to check whether the 500 was specific to this one case's data.

Identical bare 500 on TC-54456 (a different case in the same folder). Confirms the failure is not specific to one case's attachment data and fires on any well-formed request, matching the capability's own guidance verbatim. No further attempts made - varying valid ids further would not surface a fix for a pre-serialization handler bug.

notes: describeCapability's own guidance already states: 'DOES NOT WORK. Returns a bare 500 on any request. The handler calls a collection method on a value that is a plain array on this path, so it raises before serialising.' This was verified live and holds: two well-formed requests (project_id=379335744, folder_id=764093, test_case_id=1971631 then 1971632 - the latter resolved from TC-54455/TC-54456 via list_folder_test_cases_v1 since this v1 route needs integer ids) both returned HTTP 500 with an identical bare body {"status":500,"error":"Internal Server Error"}. This is a SECOND, separate defect beyond the 500 itself: describeCapability declares a structured error envelope for its 500 response ({success:false, error:{code, message, details}}), but the live body is bare - no `success`, no `error` object, no `code`/`message`/`details` fields at all, just top-level `status` and `error` (a string, not an object). The response shape does not match the capability's own declared error schema. Per the empty-case rule, since only 500s were ever observed, `declared_missing` and `undeclared_returned` are left empty - a failure body says nothing about whether the declared 200 shape (attachments[].{id, filename, content_type, byte_size}) is correct; that remains unverified. Guidance also states the v1 surface has no url/download field and folder_id is not used for lookup (only project + test_case_id) - neither could be confirmed since no 200 was ever reached. No write or destructive capability was used; list_folder_test_cases_v1 (read) was used only to resolve TC-NNNN identifiers to the integer ids this route requires.
